text: The face is the digits alone on a plain field, with the phase as one word above them, so the time reads from across the room.

angle: ring that fills over the session
text: The digits sit inside a disc whose ring fills as the interval runs, so the share of time gone reads before the numerals do.
The clock is set in monospaced type with no shapes around it, and the phase, the state and the next step come as words beneath it.
Four small marks sit under the clock and fill as work intervals finish, so the long break shows as the step that follows the fourth mark.
Each phase fills the whole screen in its own colour with the clock as the largest shape on it, so the phase reads from the far side of a room before any word is read.
When an interval ends the clock holds at zero on a still face, and the next phase waits for one press, so the person sets the pace of each break.
